To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
marital status is associated with cardiovascular risk factors and that different marital groups benefit from different primary cardiovascular prevention programs.

(1) the never-married, separated/divorced, widowed, and married groups have significantly different rates of heart attack/stroke hospitalization; (2) these groups also have different levels of cardiovascular risk factors, and these differences are not entirely explained by differences in socioeconomic status, education, age, and sex; and (3) these findings suggest that marital status is an important variable for identifying, understanding, altering, and preventing cardiovascular risk.
the separated/divorced have a higher risk of heart attack/stroke than the married and that the widowed have intermediate risk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of marital status on health, with a particular emphasis on cardiovascular disease.
identifying the social, psychological and cultural factors that influence health behaviors and outcomes.
understanding the relationship between marital status, health, and risk behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
marital status is a significant predictor of cardiovascular risk, but that the specific risk characteristics that underlie the association vary by marital group.
married persons are at lower risk for cardiovascular disease than separated/divorced persons.
marital status, in and of itself, is not a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the marital status of an individual is an important determinant of his or her cardiovascular risk.
marital status is an important variable in understanding the epidemiology of coronary heart disease.
the never married are the healthiest, the married are intermediate and the divorced/separated have the highest risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
marriage is a good thing, but not because it protects you from heart disease.
marital status is not a simple indicator of risk.
marital status is an important factor to take into account when designing and evaluating cardiovascular disease risk reduction interventions.
